title: QA Evidence by Change Type
eyebrow: Design for approval · house-rules plugin · nothing built yet
approval: Design approved: QA evidence by change type

short.lead: The QA page for the Ophan in the sky (PlunderSpell pull request 445) covered animation, enemy behaviour, a model change and co-op, yet it carried no clip, no picture and no before and after, and its change list said "0 files, +0 −0". The evidence existed: the pull request itself commits at least 48 screenshots and a clip of the wings-spread pose (docs/art/anim/fear/ophan_spread.mp4), counted from the first 100 of its changed files. The page builder let a page through that showed none of them. This design makes every QA page prove each change with the evidence its type needs, and refuses to build the page, or to let the handover reply end, until that evidence is attached.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: search
What went wrong
Seven gaps, all found in the plugin's own code
PlunderSpell's page-style.json says pictures are required, but make_page.py checks that rule only on Changes items the author marks visual. The Ophan page marked none, so the rule never ran.
All the work sat in the In short steps, and the builder checks no pictures there at all.
The page template can show images only: there is no way to put a video clip on a QA page.
Nothing knows what kind of change was made, so nothing can ask for a clip for animation or a recording for enemy behaviour.

The page named screenshots as text ("Screenshot: docs/generated/ophan-418/staging-beam-host.png") instead of showing them, and the builder doesn't notice. The committed clip ophan_spread.mp4 was never mentioned at all.
The file count was taken against staging after the feature was already merged into it, so git found no difference and the builder printed "0 files" without complaint.
The end-of-reply check only asks that a QA page is built and linked. It never asks whether the page proves anything.
Nothing from you.
list
Evidence by type
Each change declares its type and what it needs
Animation: a clip of the animation, plus a before and after.
Model: a picture of the change, plus a before and after picture.
Gameplay, or enemy AI and behaviour: a recording of it in play, plus a before and after clip.
Other visible changes, such as interface or effects: a picture plus a before and after, as the current rule already asks.
A change with nothing to see, such as a test or a script: allowed only with a sentence saying why nothing is visible.
Nothing from you.
stop
Blocked until proven
No build, and no handover reply, without it
make_page.py refuses to build a QA page when any change is missing the evidence its type needs, when a named file doesn't exist, or when the git count finds no changed files.
It also refuses a screenshot or clip path that is named in the text but not shown on the page.
The end-of-reply check accepts a QA page only when make_page.py recorded that the evidence passed, so a page published by hand no longer counts.
Nothing from you.
eye
The QA page
Clips and comparisons you can watch
Each change gets its own card with its type, the clip or picture, and a before and after shown side by side.
Before and after clips play together, so you can watch the same moment in both.
The change list is counted against the commit before the feature was merged, so it lists the real files.
Nothing from you.
hand
Your QA
You test only after you have seen it
you
You watch the clips and comparisons first, then play it yourself, then answer from the page.
You read the page and send "QA passed: <feature>" or "QA failed: <feature>" with what to change.

changes: keep
The QA page and its checkpoint
The QA stage, the QA page and "QA passed" stay as they are.
Nothing here adds a stage or a new reply. The QA mode in make_page.py, the stage file it writes and the end-of-reply "qa page" check already exist; this design gives them evidence to enforce.
chg
Picture rule in make_page.py
Becomes an evidence rule, checked on every QA change.
Pictures are checked only on Changes items an author marks visual, and only when the project's style file says pictures are required.
Every change listed in the QA block is checked against the evidence its type needs, in every project, whatever the style file says.
The style file's pictures setting keeps its meaning for design and plan pages.
new
Evidence list in the QA block
A new qa.evidence list in the content file.

Each entry names the change, its type (animation, model, gameplay, ai, visual or none), and its files: a clip or picture, and a before and after. A type of none needs a reason. The builder copies every file next to the page, as it does pictures today.
The QA block has feature, base, unverified and files.
It also has evidence: one entry per change, each with its proof attached.
You see each change's proof on the page instead of a sentence about it.
chg
Page template
Learns to show video clips.
Pictures and before and after pictures only.
Clips too, with before and after clips shown side by side and played together.
Clips are MP4 or WebM files. A clip over 15 MB is refused with a note to shorten it, because the claude.ai page host refuses larger files.
chg
The change list's git count
Counted against the commit before the merge.
Counted against the base branch, which after a merge already holds the feature, so the Ophan page said 0 files.
Counted against the point where the feature left its base, and a count of 0 files refuses the build.
This makes the change list name the real files, with the type each one implies.
chg
Rule text and docs
One line in house-rules.md, plus visual-check.md and show-dont-tell.md.
The rule says a visual change gets a before and after screenshot.
It names the evidence each change type needs on a QA page, and says a QA handover is blocked until it is attached.
verify.py gains a case for each refusal, including a copy of the Ophan page's content, which must now be refused.
choices: detect
How is a change's type decided?
A
I declare it, and the builder also reads it from the changed files

A changed animator controller or animation file means animation, a changed model file means model, and a changed enemy script means AI and behaviour. The path patterns live in each project's page-style.json. I can add types but can't drop one the files imply.
B
I declare it, and nothing double-checks
Simpler, but the Ophan page shows that an author can leave things out.
With A, pull request 445's changed TheOphanOfHours.controller and its new scripts under Scripts/Runtime/Raid/Ophan could not have reached you without a clip and a recording, whatever I wrote.
compare
What counts as a before and after for animation and gameplay?
A
Two clips side by side, playing together
You watch the same moment old and new.
B
One clip of the new version, plus a still picture of the old one
Faster for me to capture, but you can't compare the motion.
You asked for a before and after clip for gameplay, and motion is what changed.
escape
Can a QA page ever go out without the evidence?
A
Never: a change I can't capture isn't ready for QA
If I can't record it, I say so and stay in Build.
B
Only if you type "QA without evidence: <feature>" yourself
Leaves you a way through for a change you are happy to test blind.
You said to prove the work first and test it yourself only after.

wrapup.summary: Make every QA page prove each change with the evidence its type needs, and block the QA handover until that evidence is attached.
